08-031.r: Atal Tunnel (Rohtang, 9.02 km) → built by BRO across the Pir Panjal range; links Manali and Lahaul-Spiti; cuts Manali–Leh distance by 46 km; strategic. All four correct.

08-033.r: Atal Tunnel (9.02 km) → Eastern Pir Panjal range; world's longest highway tunnel above 10,000 feet, but not the longest overall (Norway's Laerdal Tunnel, 24.51 km).

08-035.r: Kashmir Valley → between the Pir Panjal (south-west) and the Great Himalaya/Himadri (north-east).

08-037.r: Aksai Chin (about 38000 sq km in Ladakh; Indian territory occupied by China) → part of the Ladakh Plateau.

08-038.r: Great Himalaya → average height about 6000 m; highest peak Everest about 8850 m (new joint Nepal–China height 8848.86 m).

08-039.r: Himachal → Middle Himalaya; average width 50 km, height 3700–4500 m; hill stations Shimla, Nainital, Mussoorie lie here.

08-040.r: Only statement 3 is correct: Pulicat Lake spans two states. Wrong: Himalayas in five states only (they cover many more); Western Ghats in five states only.

08-041.r: Indian Himalayan Region → HP, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, J&K, Ladakh, plus hills of Assam and WB; not Uttar Pradesh (only plains).

08-042.r: Youngest range among the options → Himalayas (young fold mountains; Great Himalaya = Himadri); Aravalli is India's oldest range.

08-043.r: Youngest mountain range among the options → Himadri (Great Himalaya), a new fold mountain; Aravalli is India's oldest.

08-044.r: Himalayas have the most seismic zones in India (mostly zones IV and V) because of many longitudinal thrust zones → A and R true; R explains A.

08-045.r: Imphal Basin (Manipur hills) → lacustrine plain: a plain built by sediment in a former lake; Kashmir valley is another example.

08-046.r: Correct: marine fossils in Lesser Himalayan sedimentary rocks; remains of human civilization in the Shiwalik. Wrong: Greater Himalayan sedimentary rocks are fossil-less (they have fossils).

08-047.r: Karewa ('Vuhr' locally) → plateau-like terraces above the plains of the Jhelum and its tributaries, in the Kashmir Himalaya.

08-048.r: Correct: Karewa → Kashmir Himalaya; Namcha Barwa → Arunachal; Valley of Flowers → Himachal-Uttarakhand Himalaya. Wrong: Nalagarh Dun is largest (Dehra Dun is the largest Dun).

08-049.r: Mount Kailash → in Tibet (China); a holy pilgrimage site of Hinduism.

08-050.r: Cho Oyu and Lhotse → in the Himalayas; Annamalai and Sirumali are not Himalayan ranges.

09-001.r: Oldest mountain range of India → Aravalli (Rajasthan); Precambrian fold range, about 570 million years old; highest peak Guru Shikhar (1722 m).

09-006.r: Aravalli Range → about 570 million years old (Proterozoic era); one of the world's oldest ranges.

09-007.r: Oldest geographical region of India → Indian Peninsular Plateau, formed from Gondwana Land.

09-008.r: Residual mountain → remnant of old mountains worn down by denudation; example Aravalli (not Himalaya, Kilimanjaro or Etna).

09-009.r: Highest peak of South India/Peninsula → Anaimudi (2,695 m), Western Ghats, Idukki–Ernakulam, Kerala.

09-012.r: Satpura Range ('Seven Folds') → watershed between Narmada (north) and Tapti (south); runs from eastern Gujarat along the Maharashtra–MP border to Chhattisgarh.

09-013.r: Hills north to south → Nallamalai (between Krishna and Pennar) → Javadi (Vellore–Tiruvannamalai, TN) → Nilgiri (where the Ghats meet) → Anaimalai.

09-014.r: West to east → Mahadeo → Maikal (both eastward extensions of Satpura) → Chotanagpur Plateau (Jharkhand) → Khasi Hills (Meghalaya).

09-015.r: Eastern and Western Ghats meet at the Nilgiri Hills ('Blue Mountains'); highest peak Doddabetta (about 2637 m).

09-016.r: Nilgiri Hills → between and joining the Sahyadri (Western Ghats) and Eastern Ghats; Doddabetta peak is in the Nilgiris.

09-020.r: Eastern and Western Ghats meet → Nilgiri Hills; peak Doddabetta (2637 m), second-highest in South India.
09-020.h: Nilgiri = 'Blue Mountains', the knot that ties both Ghats.

09-021.r: Nilgiri Hills → part of the Western Ghats at the junction of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu (mainly Tamil Nadu).

09-023.r: Raman Sagar mountain → 1505 m high undersea mountain in the Arabian Sea, about 455 km west-south-west of Mumbai; named after C.V. Raman.

09-024.r: Wrong: Western Ghats are higher in the north (highest peak Anaimudi, 2695 m, is in the south). True: Tapti lies south of Satpura; Narmada and Tapti are rift valleys.

09-025.r: Range in only one state → Ajanta (Maharashtra); Aravalli, Satpura and Sahyadri cross several states.

09-026.r: Western Ghats → called Sahyadri in Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka; average height 1200 m.

09-027.r: South to north → Satmala hills (Maharashtra), Kaimur hills (MP–UP–Bihar), Naga hills (Indo-Myanmar border), Pir Panjal (J&K–HP).

09-028.r: Cardamom Hills (Western Ghats) → Kerala–Tamil Nadu border (south-east Kerala, south-west Tamil Nadu); named after cardamom grown there.

09-029.r: Southernmost mountain range of India → Cardamom Hills (Yela Mala), Western Ghats in Kerala–Tamil Nadu; also grow pepper and coffee.

09-030.r: 'Yela Mala' → traditional name of the Cardamom Hills, from cardamom cultivation.

09-031.r: Shevaroy Hills → Salem district, Tamil Nadu; about 4000–5000 feet high; hill station Yercaud.

09-032.r: Mandav Hills → Gujarat (not Maharashtra); Balaghat Range, Harishchandra Range and Satmala Hills → Maharashtra.

09-033.r: Wrong pair: Mandav Hills–Maharashtra (they are in Gujarat). Correct: Garhjat Hills → Odisha; Nallamalai → Andhra Pradesh (and Telangana); Shevaroy → Tamil Nadu.

09-034.r: Correct: Mahadeo Hills → Central India; Mikir Hills → North-East India. Wrong: Cardamom (Western Ghats) – Coromandel Coast; Kaimur (MP–UP–Bihar) – Konkan Coast.

09-035.r: Mahadeo Hills → part of the Satpura range, which runs south of and parallel to the Vindhyas.

09-036.r: Dhupgarh → highest peak of the Satpura Range, at Pachmarhi (MP).

09-037.r: Ramgiri hills → in the Maikal Range (part of Satpura); also in Peddapalli, Telangana (Eastern Ghats). CGPSC's revised key took Satpura. The book gives no single answer (*).

09-038.r: Parasnath Hill → about 1365 m, Giridih district, Jharkhand; Jain Shikharji temple; named after Parasnath, the 23rd Tirthankara.

09-039.r: Garo → Meghalaya; Miri → Arunachal Pradesh; Kollai Mallai → Tamil Nadu; Dalma → Jharkhand.

09-040.r: Western Ghats (about 1500 km) → block mountain; steep western slope, gently sloping eastern plateau; northern part covered by basalt lava. All three correct.

09-041.r: Kodaikanal → in the Palni Hills, Dindigul district, Tamil Nadu.
09-041.t: Don't place Kodaikanal in the Anaimalai; it is in the Palni Hills.

09-042.r: Mukandara hills → extension of the Vindhyan ranges in Rajasthan.

09-043.r: Salher (Nashik, Maharashtra; 1,567 m; highest fort in the Sahyadri) → not in the Eastern Ghats, unlike Gali Konda, Sinkram Gutta, Madugula Konda.

09-044.r: Highest peaks: Kerala → Anaimudi; Nagaland → Saramati; Uttarakhand → Nanda Devi; Tamil Nadu → Doddabetta.

09-045.r: Central Indian hills west to east → Satpura, Mahadeo, Maikal, Chotanagpur.

09-046.r: Satpura region west to east → Barwani Hills → Mahadeo Range → Maikal Range.
09-046.h: B, Mah, Mai: alphabetical order runs west to east.

09-047.r: Hills closest to Kanyakumari → Cardamom Hills (Western Ghats; south-east Kerala and south-west Tamil Nadu).

09-048.r: Western Ghats north to south → Sahyadri (Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka) → Nilgiri → Anaimalai → Cardamom Hills.
09-048.h: 'SNAC' going south: Sahyadri, Nilgiri, Anaimalai, Cardamom.

09-049.r: No tea plantations → Girnar hills; tea grows in Kanan Devan (near Munnar, Idukki, Kerala; from the 1870s), Nilgiri and Darjeeling.

09-050.r: Bateshwar Hill → Bihar (Bhagalpur); Bilari (Bellary) Range → Karnataka; Chin Range → Manipur; Dhoshi Hill → Haryana (Mahendragarh).

09-051.r: All three wrong: Amarkantak is where Vindhya and Satpura meet (not Sahyadri); Biligirirangan Hills are in south-east Karnataka; Seshachalam Hills are Eastern Ghats (south Andhra Pradesh).

10-001.r: Only pair 2 correct: Nanda Devi–Kumaon Himalaya (Nanda Devi East is on the Chamoli–Pithoragarh–Bageshwar border). Wrong: Namcha Barwa (Tibet)–Garhwal; Nokrek–Sikkim Himalaya.

10-002.r: Mount Everest ('Sagarmatha' in Nepal) → world's highest peak, on the Nepal–China (Tibet) border; 8848 m, new height 8848.86 m. The book gives no single answer (*).

10-004.r: First Indian woman to climb Everest → Bachendri Pal (1984).

10-005.r: First woman to climb Everest → Junko Tabei of Japan (16 May 1975); also first woman to climb the highest peaks of all seven continents.

10-006.r: Santosh Yadav → first woman to climb Everest twice (May 1992, May 1993); second Indian woman on Everest after Bachendri Pal (1984).

10-008.r: Highest peak of India → K2 (Godwin Austin), Karakoram range, Ladakh; 8611 m; world's second highest.

10-010.r: Everest 8848 m (Nepal–Tibet) > K2/Godwin Austin 8611 m (India) > Kanchenjunga 8598 m (Sikkim–Nepal) > Makalu 8463 m (Nepal). Without K2 in options → Kanchenjunga.
10-010.t: If K2 is an option it is India's highest; Kanchenjunga wins only when K2 is missing.

10-013.r: Nanda Devi (7817 m) → Garhwal Himalaya; India's fourth-highest peak after K2 (8611 m), Kanchenjunga (8598 m) and Nanga Parbat.

10-014.r: Nanda Devi (7817 m, Great Himalaya) → Uttarakhand; fourth-highest in India; Nanda Devi National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1988).

10-016.r: East to west → Garo Hills (Meghalaya), Nanda Devi, Kamet (both Uttarakhand), K2 (Karakoram, Ladakh).

10-017.r: Guru Shikhar (1722 m) → highest peak of the Aravalli, in Sirohi district, Rajasthan.

10-018.r: Aravalli's highest peak is Guru Shikhar; among Sajjangarh, Lilagarh, Kumbhalgarh, Taragarh the highest → Kumbhalgarh (1224 m).

10-019.r: Ascending height → Panchmarhi 1067 m < Mahendragiri 1501 m < Guru Shikhar 1722 m < Anaimudi 2695 m.

10-020.r: Himalayan peaks east to west → Namcha Barwa (Tibet), Kanchenjunga (Sikkim/Nepal), Everest (Nepal–Tibet), Nanda Devi (Uttarakhand).

10-021.r: Gosainthan → in Tibet near the Nepal border (not India); Nanda Devi, Kamet and Trishul → Uttarakhand.

10-022.r: Not matched: Kodaikanal–Annamalai (Kodaikanal is in the Palni Hills) and Shimla–Pir Panjal, so no single answer (*). Correct: Mount Abu–Aravalli; Ootacamund–Nilgiri.

10-023.r: Peaks not in India → Gurla Mandhata and Namcha Barwa (Tibet, China); Kamet and Nanga Parbat are in India. The book accepts both (a) and (b).

10-024.r: Not in India → Dhaulagiri (Nepal). Kamet → Uttarakhand; Nanga Parbat → Ladakh; Namcha Barwa → Tibet near Arunachal border (NCERT places it in Arunachal).

10-025.r: Gaurlata peak → Samri Pat, Balrampur-Ramanujganj district; highest peak of Chhattisgarh.

10-026.r: Highest peaks: Tamil Nadu → Doddabetta; Rajasthan → Guru Shikhar; Nagaland → Saramati; Madhya Pradesh → Dhupgarh.

10-028.r: Trishul peaks (I 7120 m, II 6690 m, III 6008 m) → Bageshwar district, Uttarakhand; none exceeds 7500 m, so only statement 1 is correct.

11-001.r: Kullu Valley (Himachal Pradesh) → between the Dhauladhar and Pir Panjal ranges.

11-002.r: Kashmir Valley → geologically a tectonic valley, shaped by erosion and deposition. Commission took 'Erosional'; 'Tectonic' also fits. The book gives no single answer (*).

11-003.r: Nelang Valley → Gangotri National Park, Uttarkashi district, Uttarakhand; near India–China border; closed after the 1962 war, reopened to tourists in 2015.

11-004.r: Markha Valley → Ladakh (then J&K); Dzukou Valley → Nagaland (and Manipur), near Kohima; Sangla Valley → Kinnaur, Himachal Pradesh; Yumthang Valley → Sikkim.

11-005.r: Silent Valley National Park (Palakkad–Malappuram, Kerala) → Nilgiri Hills, not Nallamalai; Pathrakkadavu hydro project proposed nearby; Kunthi river rises in its rainforests.

11-007.r: Galwan river/valley → named after Ghulam Rassul Galwan, a Ladakhi explorer who wrote 'Servant of Sahibs' in English. All three correct.

11-008.r: Shaksgam Valley → Pakistan illegally ceded 5180 sq km of it to China (1963 'Boundary Agreement'); strategic; India protests China's construction there. Both statements correct.

11-009.r: 'Molassis Basin' → Mizoram, made of unconsolidated sediments; hilly north-eastern state; common language Lushai.

12-001.r: Wrong pair: Se La–Uttarakhand (Se La is in Arunachal Pradesh). Correct: Chang La → Ladakh (then J&K); Rohtang → Himachal Pradesh; Bomdi La → Arunachal Pradesh.

12-002.r: Palghat (Kerala) → between the Nilgiris (north) and Annamalai Hills (south); Thalghat, Bhorghat and Palghat are the main Western Ghats passes.

12-003.r: Wrong pair: Bhorghat–Himachal Pradesh; Bhorghat is in Maharashtra (Mumbai–Pune). Correct: Bomdi La → Arunachal; Nathu La → Sikkim; Palghat → Kerala.

12-004.r: Not a Western Ghats pass → Khyber Pass (Pakistan–Afghanistan border). Western Ghats: Thalghat (Mumbai–Nashik), Bhorghat (Mumbai–Pune), Palghat (Palakkad–Coimbatore).
12-004.h: North to south 'Thal-Bhor-Pal': Thalghat, Bhorghat, Palghat.

12-005.r: Wrong pair: Lipulekh–Uttar Pradesh; Lipulekh is on the India–China border in Uttarakhand. Correct: Shipki La → HP; Nathu La → Sikkim; Zojila → Kashmir.

12-006.r: Wrong pair: Nathu La–Meghalaya; Nathu La is on the India–China border in Sikkim. Correct: Shipki La → HP; Bomdi La → Arunachal; Zoji La → J&K.

12-007.r: Wrong pair: Zoji La–Arunachal; Zoji La links Kashmir Valley with Kargil–Drass and Ladakh (Ladakh UT). Correct: Sin La → Uttarakhand; Nathu La → Sikkim; Shipki La → HP.

12-008.r: Only pair 1 wrong: Lipulekh is in Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand (India–Nepal–China tri-junction), not Ladakh. Correct: Nathu La → Sikkim; Bomdila → Arunachal; Shipki La → HP.

12-009.r: Nathu La → Sikkim, 4310 m, 55 km east of Gangtok, opens into Chumbi Valley (Tibet); one of three India–China trade posts with Shipki La and Lipulekh.
12-009.h: Trade posts west to east: Shipki La (HP), Lipulekh (Uttarakhand), Nathu La (Sikkim).

12-010.r: Pass leading to Leh → Zojila (Ladakh), on National Highway-1 between Uri and Leh.

12-011.r: Zoji-la Tunnel (under construction beneath Zojila Pass, Ganderbal–Drass) → all-weather road link between Srinagar and Leh.

12-012.r: Nathu La → reopened in 2006 for India–China trade; it had been closed after the 1962 war.

12-013.r: Banihal → Jammu and Kashmir; Nathu La → Sikkim; Niti → Uttarakhand (Uttaranchal); Shipki La → Himachal Pradesh.

12-014.r: Bum La → Arunachal Pradesh; Jelep La → Sikkim; Muling La → Uttarakhand; Shipki La → Himachal Pradesh.

12-015.r: Mana → Uttarakhand; Nathu La → Sikkim; Zozi La → Jammu and Kashmir (now Ladakh UT); Shipki La → Himachal Pradesh.

12-016.r: Wrong pair: Shipki La–Jammu and Kashmir; Shipki La (Indo-China border post) is in Kinnaur, Himachal Pradesh. Correct: Jelep La → Sikkim; Mana, Niti → Uttarakhand.

12-017.r: Correct pair: Niti–Uttarakhand. Mana → Uttarakhand (not HP); Diphu → Arunachal Pradesh (not Ladakh); Aghil → Ladakh (not Arunachal).

12-018.r: Lipulekh → Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand; entry to Mansarovar via Kailash. Jelep La and Nathu La → Sikkim; Shipki La → Himachal Pradesh.

12-020.r: Wrong pair: Nathu La–Arunachal Pradesh (it is in Sikkim). Correct: Lipulekh → Uttarakhand; Rohtang → Himachal Pradesh; Palghat → Kerala.

12-022.r: Mana Pass (Dungri La) → India–Tibet border, Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve, Uttarakhand; its Deotal lake is the source of the Saraswati (Alaknanda tributary).

12-023.r: Kingri-Wingri and Neeti-Mana → Himalayan passes in Uttarakhand; Neeti links Uttarakhand to Tibet; Mana is also called Dungri La.

12-024.r: Passes west to east → Shipki La (HP), Lipulekh (Uttarakhand), Nathu La (Sikkim), Bomdi La (Arunachal).
12-024.h: Follow the states west to east: HP → Uttarakhand → Sikkim → Arunachal.

12-025.r: Heights: Nathu La about 4310 m > Rohtang 3978 m > Zojila 3528 m > Khyber 1070 m. The book picks (e), citing Yangzi Diwan as India's highest pass.
12-025.c: The book's own figures make Nathu La the highest of the four listed passes; its answer (e) rests on Yangzi Diwan, which is not an option.

12-026.r: Pass heights: Debsa 5360 m; Bara-lacha 4850 m (about 4890 m); Rohtang 3978 m (all Himachal Pradesh); Banihal 2832 m (J&K).

13-001.r: Himalayan snow line → about 4300–6000 m; average 5500–6000 m in the northern part and 4500–6000 m in the southern part.

13-002.r: Uttar Pradesh has no snow line: no snowfall after Uttarakhand separated. No option fits; the question was deleted. The book gives no single answer (*).

13-003.r: Siachen Glacier → Eastern Karakoram, north of Nubra Valley; world's highest battlefield; separates Pakistan and China in the region.

13-004.r: Largest among Siachen, Baltoro, Chogo Lungma, Biafo → Siachen (about 1056.42 sq km).

13-005.r: Longest among the options → Gangotri (30.0 km); Rundun 19 km, Kanchenjunga 16 km, Kedarnath 14.5 km.

13-006.r: Largest glacier in India → Siachen (about 72 km long as per Indian textbooks); bigger than Gangotri, Zemu, Sasaini.

13-007.r: Largest glacier of the Trans-Himalaya → Siachen (Karakoram range); Trans-Himalaya includes Karakoram, Ladakh, Zanskar and Kailash ranges.

13-008.r: Chaurabari Glacier (Garhwal, Uttarakhand) → north of Kedarnath temple; its meltwater forms Gandhi Sarovar lake.

13-009.r: Himalayan glaciers melt at the highest rate in the world; Gangotri glacier (source of the Ganga) has shrunk to half its extent in the last 50 years.

13-010.r: Milam Glacier → Kumaun region, Uttarakhand; source of the Gori Ganga river.

13-011.r: Correct: Bandarpunch → Yamuna; Bara Shigri → Chenab; Siachen → Nubra. Wrong: Mandakini rises from Chorabari (not Milam); Zemu (Sikkim, 26 km) does not feed Manas.

13-012.r: Glaciers by length, longest first → Hispar > Biafo > Drang Drung > Sonapani > Bara Shigri.

14-001.r: Deccan Trap basalt lava → Cretaceous period; coal of the Damodar, Son, Mahanadi and Godavari basins → Carboniferous period.
